Occurrences.Kwic: 因中也設問，眾荅之，不愜師意，故書偈示眾曰：秪因日起明中暗
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB188.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Rujiu Ruibai (入就瑞白禪師語錄): Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Ruibai (入就瑞白禪師語錄): Ruibai Mingxue writes a verse to address the assembly.

Senses.Explanation: As a record heading and speech frame, the phrase means to address or instruct the assembled community. Yuanwu Keqin ascends the seat and addresses the assembly; Huangbo Xiyun’s instruction begins with the same frame; Luopu Yuanan uses it for a final question before death; Vasumitra emerges from concentration and addresses the assembly about the teaching he obtained. Yuejiang Zhengyin explicitly calls the daytime drum-and-hall event “addressing the assembly” and says its content is not inherently different from the night small convocation. The formula can therefore label a public speech event even when the following words differ in genre or occasion.

Senses.Note: Four concrete display witnesses from four independent works establish the action sense.

Senses.Explanation: With a concrete object and a gesture verb, the headword keeps its compositional action sense: to show something to the assembly. Shakyamuni holds up a flower before the assembly; Yuanwu raises a whisk and asks whether the assembly sees it; Yaoshan Weiyan lifts donated trousers and asks whether the teaching body possesses the four elements; Yangshan Huiji lifts a letter and mirror sent by Guishan. Here the object, not a resulting discourse, controls the event.
